reuse.why: Extends the existing WeekendRule helpers (isSkippedWeekendOccurrence, getDateWithSkippedWeekend) that getNextDate, getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange and the template code already call, and turns the hard-coded search window into a shared function.

duplication.why: The holiday test is defined once in isNonWorkingDay and used by both the skip and the move paths; getUpcomingDates' local count * 7 is replaced by the shared window helper.

placement.why: All rule logic stays in shared/schedules.ts and the holidays field rides on the existing WeekendRule/parsed schedule data.

scope.why: Only the rule helpers, the data field, the window and tests are touched.

maintainability.why: Clean centralised rule; the one gap is getDatesInRange's local two-day margin, which still encodes the old maximum shift and was not routed through the new window logic.

one_place.where: isNonWorkingDay in shared/schedules.ts, used by isSkippedWeekendOccurrence, getDateWithSkippedWeekend and getNextDate's candidate search, which every schedule date path calls (getDatesInRange's lookup margin remains a separate local constant)
